entries.golden_scenario: Operator, 2026-07-30: 'I'm guessing you're still not retriggering yourself after the limits reset. How do we make that actually work?' The machine-local predecessor (~/.claude/state/limit-resume/resume.sh, never in this repo) required a manual `touch` to arm — the moment a usage limit actually kills a session is exactly the moment no one is present to arm it, so the watchdog had never once fired successfully in production despite existing for some time. This entry replaces it: scripts/limit-resume.sh (arm/disarm/tick/status) is auto-armed via a SessionStart splice (session-start-digest.sh) AND a new UserPromptSubmit hooks[] entry (turn-scoped re-arm — Stop fires per-turn, not per-session, so session-only arming would protect just the first turn), auto-disarmed via a Stop splice (workstreams-stop-writer.sh), installed via scripts/install-limit-resume.sh (idempotent macOS LaunchAgent, StartInterval 900s). SCOPE BOUNDARY (harness-reviewer REJECT round 3, PROVEN the original text overclaimed this): the liveness allowlist (see fp_expectation) proceeds ONLY on hb_classify's `crashed` verdict — a CONFIRMED-DEAD process. This mechanism therefore resumes ONLY the subset of usage-limit events that actually KILL the process; an alive session whose API traffic is merely erroring (`throttled` — a limit PAUSE the CLI is already retrying internally) is deliberately never touched here, matching ADR-061 D4's own explicit never-spawn rule for exactly that class. That `throttled`-alive subset has no live auto-resume coverage in this repo at all (ADR-061's own deferral ladder for it remains deliberately unarmed) — a real, named, currently-uncovered gap, not silently folded into this entry's scope.
entries.fp_expectation: harness-reviewer REJECT (2026-07-30) PROVED the original design's tick had NO liveness discriminator: since the marker is armed exactly while a turn is in flight, a tick landing seconds after arm would spawn `claude -p --resume` against a LIVE, healthy, mid-turn session and then delete the marker on the (also live) success — the per-turn false-positive probability was near-certain for any turn over ~15min. Fixed with two independent gates BOTH required before any attempt: (a) a MIN_SILENCE_SECONDS floor (default 1800s/30min, matching ADR-061 D4's own cooldown floor) — deterministic, works with zero heartbeat coverage; (b) hooks/lib/session-heartbeat-lib.sh's hb_classify (the SAME canonical oracle session-resumer.sh already uses) — a heartbeat classified `live` blocks the attempt regardless of the floor; hb_is_stale is already transcript-mtime-aware for the 'heartbeats only refresh at Stop' mid-turn case, so a long real turn is correctly read as still-live. Self-tests S11 (floor alone blocks an immediate post-arm tick, reproducing the reviewer's own probe) and S12/S13 (a live heartbeat fixture blocks; a stale/crashed one proceeds) are standing regression tests for exactly this class. Separately, state is now keyed PER SESSION ($STATE_DIR/armed/<key>.*, not one machine-global marker — reviewer finding F3, PROVEN two concurrent sessions in different repos would otherwise clobber each other; self-test S14), and arm/disarm remain no-ops from any cwd that is not the main checkout (self-tested S2/S8, now asserting the worktree setup itself succeeded first — reviewer finding F5 caught the prior versions of these two tests passing vacuously when `git worktree add` failed). Remaining bounded risk: exactly one concurrent spawn machine-wide (mkdir lock), bounded retries (default 8) with real backoff, hard stop with a visible giveup sentinel (self-test S6 is mutation-proof: pins the stub call count at MAX_RETRIES across further ticks). ROUND 2 (harness-reviewer REJECT again on the round-1 fixes, same day, 2 more Critical findings PROVEN via concurrency/classification probes): the liveness gate was still a DENY-list ('proceed unless live'), so it spawned on `throttled` (ADR-061 D4's own explicit never-spawn class -- an alive, internally-retrying limit-paused session) and on `stale` (a healthy, merely-idle session); fixed by inverting to an ALLOWLIST -- proceed ONLY on `crashed` (confirmed-dead pid), everything else skips (self-test S15). Separately, `disarm` used to unconditionally `rmdir` the GLOBAL spawn lock even when a DIFFERENT session's tick was actively holding it mid-spawn (disarm fires on every turn's Stop, for every tracked session) -- the reviewer measured two concurrent `claude` children against the same session; fixed by never releasing the lock from disarm at all (only the owning tick's own EXIT trap, or an age-based stale-lock reclaim at TIMEOUT_SECONDS+120s, ever removes it -- self-tests S16/S17). Also fixed: the floor check used to fail OPEN (skip the floor entirely) on an unparseable armed_at; now fails closed. ROUND 4 (harness-reviewer REJECT a fourth time, PROVEN via a real concurrency probe measuring 2 live children): round 2's disarm-side lock-ownership fix was not generalized to the other two lock-touching paths -- age-based stale-lock reclaim could steal the lock from a still-ALIVE owner (proven: a GNU `timeout`-bounded child that traps/ignores TERM can outlive TIMEOUT_SECONDS while legitimately still running), and the EXIT trap removed whatever sat at the lock path with no ownership check, so a tick whose lock was reclaimed would then delete the reclaimer's fresh lock on its own exit. Fixed: every acquirer writes an owner-pid token at mkdir time; release and reclaim are now BOTH gated on that token (reclaim additionally requires `kill -0 <owner_pid>` to fail, i.e. confirmed death, not just age) -- self-tests S20 (a confirmed-alive owner's lock is never reclaimed, however old) and S21 (the EXIT trap never removes a lock whose owner no longer matches). "Remaining bounded risk" above now means: exactly one concurrent spawn machine-wide, enforced by ownership-scoped lock release + liveness-confirmed reclaim, not by lock age alone.

entries.chokepoint: pre-stop-verifier.sh (Stop chain) is the ONLY invoker; the executor refuses execution of curl/sql without an explicit --allow-exec flag that no hook passes, and the suite pins that env vars cannot re-arm it.
bypass_paths: (a) --allow-exec explicit opt-in — operator-invoked runs only; no hook or dispatcher passes it (suite-pinned env-cannot-re-arm-execution).
(b) UNVERIFIABLE is deliberately non-blocking — a FALSE claim written in an unknown/inexecutable format is reported but not refuted; named residual, accepted because executing it was the CRITICAL.
(c) evidence files outside the scanned docs/ surface are never parsed — same scope bound as the pre-fix gate.

(d) NAMED AND ACCEPTED — the `file` branch is a one-bit read oracle over any readable path on the machine. `_rve_resolve_path` (executor ~L184-193) deliberately resolves both absolute (`/...`) and home-relative (`~/...`) citations, and the branch reports PASS or FAIL per pattern, so an evidence line can ask 'does <any file this user can read> contain <arbitrary substring>' and recover the answer as one bit, emitted to stderr at session end. This is NOT closed, on purpose: it is the READ half of the very 'read, don't run' boundary the executor exists to enforce (the CRITICAL was EXECUTION, not reading), and the `~/.claude/...` citations that the repo's own evidence convention depends on are precisely the absolute and `~/` paths a repo-relative-only resolver would reject — closing it would make the convention's dominant evidence shape unverifiable and push authors back toward the `curl`/`command` formats that are strictly more dangerous. Bounded by: read-only (the branch has no write or exec primitive), one bit per evidence line, stderr-only at session end with no network sink, and the same docs/ scope bound as (c) — so exfiltration requires an attacker who can already both write docs/ and read the session's stderr.

entries.golden_scenario: A dispatched builder worktree crashes, is SIGKILLed/OOM-killed, or survives a machine reboot mid-turn, leaving uncommitted edits and/or a committed-but-never-cherry-picked branch behind while its liveness signal goes stale and the owning process is dead (or the machine simply never came back up) — INCLUDING a dispatched plan-phase-builder subagent (isolation:worktree, worktree named `agent-<id>`), which writes NO heartbeat of its own (only a top-level session's heartbeat writer runs), so the ORIGINAL heartbeat-only design would classify an ACTIVELY-RUNNING builder's dirty worktree as stranded on every parallel-build day (the harness-review REFORMULATE finding this entry's current fp_expectation documents the fix for) — AND, critically (harness-review ROUND-2 finding, 2026-07-17), the dispatch/isolation mechanism `git worktree lock`s an agent's worktree for the FULL duration of its dispatch, unlocking only on clean completion, so a crashed/SIGKILLed/OOM-killed agent's worktree stays `locked` FOREVER (proven on the reviewing machine: dead-pid locked worktrees persisting after the owning process is confirmed dead via `tasklist`, since `kill -0` is unreliable on that MSYS setup) — a shape the round-1 transcript-mtime fix still MISSED, because the sweep's pre-existing `*,locked,*` structural-skip returned before the liveness split ever ran for ANY locked worktree (agent or not), making the crash class this very golden_scenario field claimed to catch UNREACHABLE for the locked case specifically until this round's fix. The shared detector (scripts/worktree-hygiene-sweep.sh --stranded[--porcelain]) joins that worktree's dirty/unintegrated state against session-heartbeat-lib.sh's liveness classification (named/non-agent worktrees, locked or not — unchanged) or the agent's own transcript-mtime (agent-<id> worktrees, LOCKED OR NOT as of round 2) and surfaces it on the very next SessionStart digest (session-start-digest.sh's feed_stranded_work) and the next harness-doctor.sh --quick (check_orphaned_worktree_work), naming the worktree path, branch, dirty/unintegrated counts, and the exact salvage command (including the `git worktree unlock` step a locked row needs, since `git worktree remove` refuses on a locked worktree and a single --force is not enough) — rather than the work silently rotting until a manual `git worktree list` audit.
entries.fp_expectation: Low. REFORMULATED (2026-07-1x, docs/harness-improvements/orphaned-worktree-guard.md) after a harness-reviewer REFORMULATE verdict on the original heartbeat-only join: a dispatched plan-phase-builder subagent (isolation:worktree) writes NO heartbeat of its own, so the original design would classify an ACTIVELY-RUNNING builder's dirty `agent-<id>` worktree as stranded on every parallel-build day — a cry-wolf false positive the review correctly blocked on. Fix: for a worktree whose basename matches `agent-*` (the harness's own dispatch-time naming), `_live_owner` treats that agent's OWN transcript file mtime (`<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, appended to continuously while the agent works — verified against this session's own transcript, not assumed) as the PRIMARY liveness signal, checked before the heartbeat/claim join and requiring no dispatch-path change. ROUND 2 (harness-review, 2026-07-17): the round-1 fix above was itself found to be UNREACHABLE for a locked agent worktree — `classify_worktree`'s pre-existing `*,locked,*` structural-skip returned BEFORE the liveness split (and therefore before the transcript-mtime check) ever ran, for ANY locked worktree. Proven on the reviewing machine: the dispatch/isolation mechanism locks an agent's worktree for the full dispatch duration and only unlocks on clean completion, so THREE real dead-pid locked worktrees existed on that machine at review time, none of them ever reaching this detector's liveness logic at all. Fixed: `classify_worktree` no longer lets `locked` preempt an `agent-*`-named worktree specifically — it falls through to the normal dirty/unique computation and the liveness split, exactly as an unlocked agent worktree would, with `_live_owner` now taking a third `is_locked` argument so a stale-transcript-and-locked verdict reports the distinct label `agent-crashed-locked` (vs. plain `agent-transcript-stale` for stale-but-unlocked) — informative for salvage, since `git worktree remove` refuses on a locked worktree (a single `--force` is NOT enough; verified: `git worktree unlock <path>` first, or `git worktree remove -f -f <path>` [force TWICE], are the only ways through). A LOCKED but FRESH-transcript agent worktree is UNCHANGED-live: lock status carries no liveness information on its own (a live, actively-working agent is ALSO locked for the same reason a crashed one is) — only transcript freshness decides. Non-agent locked worktrees are UNCHANGED (still structural-skip; a manually-locked worktree, e.g. on removable media, is presumed intentionally persistent, unlike a dispatch-locked agent worktree). Also fixed in this round: `_build_agent_tx_cache`'s `find -maxdepth 6` was measured to include the Workflow-dispatch transcript variant (`.../subagents/workflows/wf_<id>/agent-<id>.jsonl`) at EXACTLY depth 6 — zero slack, the same class of silent-miss risk this whole reformulation exists to close — bumped to `-maxdepth 7`. The six mandated non-fires are now structurally guaranteed, not heuristic: (i) a still-live AGENT worktree (locked or not, as of round 2) is excluded via a transcript mtime within AGENT_TX_FRESH_MIN (default 30, same as OBS_STALE_MIN) minutes of now; (ii) a still-live NAMED (non-agent) session's worktree is excluded via the heartbeat/transcript-mtime liveness join (hb_classify live/throttled, including the mid-turn stale-heartbeat-but-fresh-transcript override, plus a CONTINUING-marker grace window for a builder standing by awaiting a scheduled wake) and the invoking session's own SELF-worktree exclusion; (iii) an already-integrated branch is excluded via git-cherry patch-equivalence PLUS merge-base --is-ancestor across all four candidate integration refs (origin/master, origin/main, master, main), so a local merge/cherry-pick that origin merely lags is never false-flagged; (iv) the orchestrator's own primary checkout is excluded twice over (the sweep's unconditional primary-skip plus the SELF check); (v) an agent-transcript cache lookup can only ADD ownership for `agent-*`-named worktrees specifically (anchored exact-basename match) — it is structurally inert for every non-agent worktree, so it can never suppress or alter the pre-existing heartbeat-based verdict for a named session; (vi) a LOCKED agent worktree that is genuinely still live is never false-flagged either — `is_locked` only ever narrows the VERDICT LABEL on an already-orphaned classification (agent-transcript-stale vs. agent-crashed-locked), it never feeds into the fresh/stale decision itself, so a live-but-locked agent takes the exact same early `agent-transcript-fresh` return path as a live-and-unlocked one. RESIDUAL (named, not eliminated — accepted for a WARN-only, never-auto-pruning surfacer): an agent that goes silent for longer than AGENT_TX_FRESH_MIN while genuinely still working (one very long reasoning/tool call with no intermediate transcript flush) could false-fire past the window; widening the window would materially delay real-orphan detection for the far more common crash/stall cases this entry exists to catch, so the tradeoff is kept at parity with the session-level OBS_STALE_MIN default rather than widened further. Also still bounded to the mode-(b) standing-by window past its grace and MSYS pid-liveness unreliability (mitigated by preferring transcript-mtime, which is platform-independent, over a pid check) — all advisory-only and non-destructive (nothing is ever auto-pruned; a locked worktree is additionally NEVER SAFE-PRUNE regardless of this fix, both because `git worktree remove` itself refuses on locked and because `classify_worktree` explicitly excludes `is_locked` from the SAFE-PRUNE promotion). worktree-hygiene-sweep.sh's own --self-test covers every excluded case explicitly (round-1: 39/39 — the original 34 live/throttled/CONTINUING-grace/fresh-claim/already-merged/self exclusions plus 5 REFORMULATION assertions for fresh/stale/unaffected-non-agent; round 2 adds 4 more proving (d) a LOCKED agent worktree with a stale transcript and content is ORPHANED with the agent-crashed-locked verdict and salvage text naming the unlock step [3 assertions], and (e) a LOCKED agent worktree with a FRESH transcript stays LIVE-OWNED, unaffected by the lock [1 assertion] — verified by an actual run: 43/43 total, 0 failed); the doctor adds its own agent-worktree fixture (oww-agent-live-green: dirty + zero heartbeat coverage + fresh transcript -> no WARN) on top of its pre-existing dirty/clean/live-owned fixtures (WARN present for a dirty orphan, absent for clean/merged/live-owned); both the doctor and the digest delegate entirely to this same detector, so they inherit both rounds' fixes with no changes of their own beyond the doctor's own fixture additions.

entries.golden_scenario: Operator mandate (2026-07-20, verbatim): "Aren't you supposed to have mechanisms in place to keep things from stopping and going stale? ... I told you to design this system so that it is continuously always making progress and never stops." Three incidents in 48h named in docs/reviews/2026-07-19-continuous-operation-design-input.md's own 'Sessions are mortal' section: the NL Observability session died of context exhaustion mid-integration (work stranded in worktrees, found only because the operator asked); a reboot killed four builders and a review batch mid-flight; a 'dead' session later REVIVED and raced the replacement orchestrator. A fourth, git-provable instance: the 2026-07-19 harness-review batch (commit aeaf9d8) returned REFORMULATE on coord-sync.sh, but the session died before persisting the finding — the fix wave landed on branch build/harness-reform-f123 and never merged, discovered only when a LATER session re-derived it from scratch weeks later (docs/reviews/2026-07-20-f1-f3-rederived-harness-review.md: "The prior fix wave ... never landed — branch empty vs origin/master"). All four instances share one root cause: the existing stranded-worktree-work detector (this manifest's own sibling entry) is ONLY consumed at SessionStart or an on-demand harness-doctor.sh --quick run — i.e. only when a session happens to be open. supervisor-tick.sh closes that gap the same way health-tick.sh (ADR-061 D6) closed it for doctor/scheduled-task/heartbeat health: a scheduled OS task fires the SAME deployed detector independent of any session being open, and durably alerts (NEEDS-YOU.md + external-monitor-alerts) the moment a worktree obligation goes orphaned — not weeks later when a human happens to notice.
entries.fp_expectation: Low, inherited: supervisor-tick.sh does NOT reimplement worktree-hygiene-sweep.sh's dirty/unintegrated/liveness classification (a second, drifting implementation of "is this owned" is exactly the class that detector's own header warns against) — it consumes that ALREADY-REVIEWED detector's --stranded --porcelain output verbatim, so it inherits that entry's own fp_expectation (agent-transcript-fresh / live / throttled / CONTINUING-grace / fresh-claim / already-merged / SELF exclusions) unchanged. This tick's OWN new false-positive surface is narrow: (1) an orphan already alerted is re-alerted only after SUPERVISOR_TICK_REALERT_HOURS (default 24h) — a per-orphan ledger (~/.claude/state/supervisor/orphans/<cksum-key>.json) makes a re-fire idempotent, so the same orphan cannot spam NEEDS-YOU.md/the alert dir on every 5-minute tick; (2) a detector or fork that hangs is bounded by a wall-clock budget (SUPERVISOR_TICK_BUDGET_SECS, default 120s) with every subprocess timeout-wrapped, so a slow/hung fork WARNS (DETECTOR_MISSING / SWEEP_TIMEOUT anomaly, reusing health-tick.sh's exact alert schema) rather than hanging the tick or the scheduled task indefinitely. Self-test (4 scenarios, 16 assertions, all against the REAL unmodified worktree-hygiene-sweep.sh as the pre-existing oracle, not a stub): fake stranded worktree + dead heartbeat -> alert fires once and stays idempotent on an immediate re-fire; a live-heartbeat-owned dirty worktree -> silent in NEEDS-YOU.md, the alert dir, AND the ledger (the FP guard); missing detector -> graceful WARN + one DETECTOR_MISSING alert, exit 0, never a crash; an orphan whose last_alerted is backdated past the TTL -> re-alerted (proves the design does not silently forget an unresolved orphan forever).

BOTH verifier dispatches (task-verifier, harness-reviewer) died instantly with 'You have hit your monthly spend limit ... to keep using Fable 5', and only ran when the caller manually passed model: opus. A verifier that dies on arrival is a verification that silently did not happen -- the same failure class that let f6562b2 reach master unreviewed. Operator: 'Fable is supposed to always fail back to Opus. That's supposed to be built in. If it's not, then fix it.' With fable marked exhausted, model-pin-gate.sh now BLOCKS a fable-pinned dispatch and names the exact override (model: opus, chain[1] from the policy file); proven end-to-end 8/8 including that an explicit opus dispatch still passes and a haiku-pinned agent is unaffected. EXTENDED 2026-08-05: model-pin-gate.sh --observe (PostToolUse Task|Agent) auto-marks a tier the FIRST time a real dispatch dies with the verbatim spend-limit error, closing the 'someone has to notice and run mark-exhausted by hand' gap. REMEDIATED 2026-08-06 (harness-change-review, both Critical, both PROVEN by replaying this session's own real transcripts): the v1 --observe grepped the trigger phrase UNANCHORED against the whole tool_response, so the phrase appearing in an Agent launch-ack's echoed `.prompt` (an OBJECT, not the terminal STRING a real death produces) or in a foreground agent's own report text fired identically to a real death -- one replay marked a SUCCESSFUL opus dispatch exhausted, another marked sonnet (categories.build.chain is [sonnet] only -- a total builder lockout). Fixed with two independent discriminators (anchored 'Error: Agent terminated early due to an API error' prefix; skip any object-shaped tool_response carrying a `prompt` key) plus a second bug where the stored reason echoed the matched trigger text itself, which dispatch-directives.sh then printed into the NEXT dispatch's prompt -- a TRUE positive could self-seed a FALSE positive one hop later. See docs/plans/model-fallback-mechanization-2026-08-05.md for the full record.

entries.honest_status: HONEST SCOPE -- this is a REROUTE, not an automatic fallback, and must not be described as one. A PreToolUse hook cannot rewrite tool input and cannot catch an API error raised after the call is admitted, so no harness-side code can transparently retry a dead Fable dispatch on Opus. What this does is convert a SILENT 100%-reproducible death into a LOUD block naming the override, which is the strongest rung actually available. PARTIALLY SELF-DETECTING as of 2026-08-05, corrected here 2026-08-06 -- an earlier version of this entry said 'there is no API to query budget, so this is not self-detecting,' which stopped being true the moment --observe (PostToolUse Task|Agent) shipped: a dispatch that dies with the verbatim 'terminated early due to an API error ... spend limit' string is now auto-marked with no manual step. This is still not a BUDGET QUERY -- there is no API to ask 'how much is left,' so the tier must actually die once, on THIS machine, before --observe can mark it; a manual `model-availability.sh mark-exhausted fable --reason ...` remains the path for exhaustion an operator learns of some other way (a UI outside this harness, a teammate's report). NOT COVERED, same as model-pin-gate's pre-existing residual: Workflow-inline agent() model:, spawn_task, and cron/remote dispatch surfaces a PreToolUse hook never sees; --observe is PostToolUse-only and, for the same reason, only ever sees the Task/Agent tool surface.
